name: Tiratricol (Triac)
summary: A thyroid-hormone analogue approved for a rare genetic disorder and once sold as an over-the-counter fat-burner.

name: Levothyroxine (T4)
summary: The standard hypothyroidism drug; users aim to correct low-normal thyroid levels for energy and a leaner look, and the label warns against weight-loss use.

name: Desiccated thyroid (Armour)
summary: Dried porcine thyroid supplying T4 and T3; people use it hoping a faster metabolism helps them get leaner.

name: Hydroxyprogesterone caproate
summary: A long-acting injectable progestin used in hormone-related care, from gynecology to feminizing hormone therapy, where progestogens are part of how some people shape their body's hormonal profile.

name: Medroxyprogesterone acetate
summary: A prescription progestin (Depo-Provera) used in feminizing hormone therapy and for hirsutism, where it shifts hormone balance and hair growth.

name: Megestrol acetate
summary: A prescription progestin appetite stimulant used in cancer and AIDS wasting; people interested in gaining weight on a thin frame discuss it for the appetite boost.

name: Cyproheptadine
summary: An allergy antihistamine that increases appetite; used off-label for weight gain in children and discussed by people trying to eat more while bulking.

name: Hexoprenaline
summary: A beta-2 agonist medicine for asthma and labour suppression, in the same class as fat-loss stimulants like clenbuterol.

name: Tulobuterol
summary: A once-daily beta-2 agonist skin patch approved in Japan for asthma, discussed in fat-loss circles as a gentler cousin of clenbuterol-type compounds.

name: Methylphenidate
summary: An ADHD stimulant whose appetite suppression leads some people to use it to eat less and lean out.

name: Amphetamine / Adderall
aka: Adderall, Adderall XR, mixed amphetamine salts
summary: A prescription stimulant that suppresses appetite; looksmaxxing forum users discuss it for eating less and leaning out.

name: Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse)
summary: A dextroamphetamine prodrug approved for ADHD and binge-eating disorder; people discuss it for its appetite-reducing effect when trying to lean out.

name: Atomoxetine
summary: A non-stimulant ADHD medication that supports steady focus and consistency with the habits behind a better physique and grooming.

name: Amantadine
summary: A prescription dopamine-boosting drug used for Parkinson's and brain-injury recovery and discussed for fatigue and drive.

name: Selegiline
summary: A prescription MAO-B inhibitor that raises brain dopamine; some people use it for mood, drive and recovery, and it is also discussed as a nootropic.

name: Galantamine
summary: A snowdrop-derived cholinesterase inhibitor that nootropic and dream communities use for cognition and vivid or lucid dreams.

name: Donepezil
summary: A prescription Alzheimer's drug that raises acetylcholine, discussed by some forum members as a memory and focus aid.

name: Rolipram
summary: A PDE4 inhibitor studied for inflammation and cognition, discussed by some for recovery, mood and memory that support training and appearance.

name: Ampakines (CX717 etc.)
summary: Experimental AMPA-receptor boosters studied for memory, attention and alertness.

name: IDRA-21
summary: A research AMPA-receptor modulator studied in animals for memory and learning, which is why it appears in nootropic circles aiming for sharper focus and recall.

name: Quinine skin bleaching
summary: Quinine appears in reports of unregulated skin-lightening products where users wanted a lighter complexion; no research describes it as a lightener.

name: Vilon
summary: A Lys-Glu dipeptide from Russian gerontology research, discussed in longevity circles as an anti-aging candidate; studied in cells and mice.

name: Pinealon
summary: A Glu-Asp-Arg tripeptide from Khavinson's lab marketed for brain and anti-aging use, with a looks link through sleep and healthy aging.

name: Thymogen
summary: A Glu-Trp dipeptide immunomodulator from Russian peptide research, discussed in longevity circles for immune and anti-aging claims.

name: Bronchogen
summary: An Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu tetrapeptide from Khavinson's lab aimed at lung tissue, discussed as an organ-specific anti-aging peptide.

name: Cardiogen
summary: An Ala-Glu-Asp-Arg tetrapeptide from Khavinson's lab aimed at heart tissue, discussed in longevity circles as an anti-aging peptide.

name: Vesugen
summary: A three-amino-acid peptide (KED) people use hoping for healthier blood vessels and a fresher, younger-looking complexion.

name: Crystagen
summary: A three-amino-acid Khavinson peptide taken for spleen and immune support as part of broader anti-aging stacks.

name: Chonluten
summary: A three-amino-acid Khavinson peptide associated with airway lining health and general wellbeing.

name: Livagen
summary: A four-amino-acid Khavinson peptide used by anti-aging enthusiasts hoping cells, and eventually looks, stay younger.

name: Thymalin
summary: A Russian calf-thymus peptide extract used for immune support and as a general anti-aging option.

name: Epithalamin
summary: The bovine pineal extract behind Epitalon, used by longevity enthusiasts hoping to slow ageing, including how old they look.

name: Cortexin
summary: A Russian cattle-brain peptide medicine used for neurological conditions and discussed as a nootropic.

name: Retinalamin
summary: An animal-derived retinal peptide extract from Russia, used for eye conditions and discussed in longevity circles for eye health.

name: Prostatilen
summary: A cattle prostate peptide extract used in post-Soviet urology and listed in longevity circles for general health.

name: Cartalax
summary: A Russian-developed three-amino-acid peptide used in the hope of supporting cartilage and joints so people can keep training and looking youthful.

name: Cortagen
summary: A Khavinson brain-derived tetrapeptide (AEDP) used by longevity enthusiasts for neural ageing and cognition.

name: Ovagen
summary: A Khavinson liver-targeted tripeptide (EDL) listed in longevity circles for liver and gut support.

name: Pancragen
summary: A Khavinson pancreas-targeted tetrapeptide used for metabolic and ageing support.

name: Prostamax
summary: A four-amino-acid Khavinson peptide modelled on prostate extract and used for prostate support in longevity circles.

name: Testagen
summary: A four-amino-acid bioregulator peptide promoted for testosterone support, which users link to a leaner, more muscular look.

name: Vesilute
summary: A Glu-Asp dipeptide bioregulator that proponents use for bladder and urinary wellness as part of a longevity routine.

name: Thymulin
summary: A zinc-dependent thymus hormone discussed in peptide and zinc circles for immune and general health.

name: Thymosin Beta-4
summary: A natural repair peptide sold as TB-500, used for tissue recovery and by hair-loss hobbyists hoping for follicle effects; banned in sport.

name: Thymosin Fraction 5
summary: The calf-thymus extract that thymosin alpha-1 and beta-4 were purified from, relevant mainly as their source.

name: Thymopentin
summary: A thymus-derived immune peptide studied for infections and skin conditions such as atopic dermatitis.

name: GHRP-3
summary: A growth hormone-releasing peptide discussed by physique enthusiasts for GH-driven muscle and leanness.

name: GHRP-4
summary: An obscure growth hormone-releasing peptide mentioned in physique forums for GH-driven muscle and fat loss.

name: GHRP-5
summary: The "Momany peptide": a GH-releasing peptide bodybuilders consider for muscle and leanness, studied in laboratory and anti-doping papers.

name: Livoletide
summary: An investigational unacylated-ghrelin peptide built to reduce hunger in Prader-Willi syndrome, discussed for appetite control and a leaner body.

name: Lenomorelin (Ghrelin)
summary: Ghrelin, the stomach hunger hormone that also stimulates growth hormone, discussed as a lever on appetite and body composition.

name: Cortistatin-14
summary: A somatostatin-related brain peptide that also binds ghrelin-type receptors, occasionally discussed for recovery and the GH axis.

name: LUM-201
summary: LUM-201 (ibutamoren) is an oral GH secretagogue that physique users discuss as a pill route to higher GH and IGF-1 for muscle and leanness.

name: IGF-1 DES
summary: A truncated IGF-1 analogue forum users inject locally hoping to grow the jaw, chin and muscle; research is in cells and animals.

name: Somatrogon
summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone for children with diagnosed GH deficiency, which raises growth velocity and comes up in height discussions.

name: Lonapegsomatropin
summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone prodrug for children and adults with diagnosed GH deficiency, mentioned in height-focused circles.

name: Somapacitan
summary: A weekly albumin-binding growth hormone for diagnosed GH deficiency and some short-stature conditions, watched by height-focused users.

name: Mecasermin
summary: Prescription recombinant IGF-1 for children with rare severe IGF-1 deficiency, raised in height forums as a growth lever.

name: Pegvisomant
summary: Prescription GH-receptor blocker for acromegaly; it lowers IGF-1 and serves as a reference point for GH-driven facial and bone change.

name: Bivamelagon
summary: Investigational oral MC4R agonist that targets the brain's appetite pathway, tested for hypothalamic obesity.

name: RM-718
summary: Experimental weekly MC4R agonist aimed at the brain's appetite pathway, in early trials for rare obesity syndromes.

name: PL-8177
summary: Experimental oral MC1r peptide linked to melanocortin pigment signalling, studied in ulcerative colitis rather than tanning.

name: SHU-9119
summary: A lab melanocortin antagonist used in rodent appetite research as a reference tool for how melanocortin signalling shapes body weight.

name: Agouti-related peptide
summary: The brain's own hunger-driving peptide that blocks satiety receptors; studied as a lever for appetite and body-fat control.

name: Atumelnant
summary: An investigational oral ACTH-pathway blocker that sharply lowers adrenal androgens in CAH, relevant to androgen-driven skin and hair changes.

name: Tetracosactide
summary: Synthetic ACTH fragment used to test adrenal function, informing cortisol-related energy and body composition.

name: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
summary: The pituitary hormone that sets cortisol output and sits in the same family as the skin-darkening melanocortins; given by prescription as corticotropin.

name: S-23
summary: A potent nonsteroidal SARM sold as a gray-market research chemical, taken for muscle gain; it was developed as a male contraceptive candidate.

name: S-40503
summary: A nonsteroidal SARM with tissue-selective androgen receptor activity, described in rat osteoporosis models and detectable in doping tests.

name: LGD-2226
summary: An experimental quinolinone SARM studied in animals for muscle and bone effects, sold as a research chemical for muscle gain.

name: LGD-2941
summary: A quinolinone SARM that muscle-building communities treat as a lean mass candidate; its development was discontinued after Phase I.

name: LGD-3303
summary: An oral nonsteroidal SARM from Ligand Pharmaceuticals discussed for muscle gain; studied in rats and horses.

name: ACP-105
summary: An experimental partial-agonist SARM that users take for lean mass with milder androgenic effects; studied in rats and mice, sold online as a research chemical.

name: AC-262536
summary: An Acadia-developed SARM that users take for lean muscle gain with smaller prostate effects; studied in rats, sold online as a research chemical.

name: BMS-564929
summary: A very potent Bristol-Myers Squibb SARM that drives muscle growth in rats with little prostate stimulation; its early human trial was discontinued.

name: GLPG0492
summary: An experimental non-steroidal SARM studied for muscle wasting that users take to build muscle with weaker prostate effects; tested in mice and phase 1 volunteer trials.

name: TFM-4AS-1
summary: A laboratory steroidal SARM that favored muscle and bone over reproductive tissue in rats; not yet studied in people.

name: MK-0773
summary: A steroidal SARM that added lean mass in frail older women in a phase 2 trial, though strength and function did not improve beyond placebo.

name: GSK2881078
summary: A pharma-developed SARM that raised lean mass in older adults and leg strength in men with COPD, with lower HDL and transient liver-enzyme rises reported.

name: OPK-88004
summary: An investigational SARM that raised lean mass and reduced fat in prostate cancer survivors, though symptoms and performance did not improve.

name: MK-3984
summary: An obscure SARM candidate aimed at muscle and bone, known mainly from a doping-control metabolite study; no human data.

name: Arcarine
summary: Orion's discontinued SARM candidate aimed at selective muscle and bone activation; reached Phase I and left almost no public data.

name: GSK-971086
summary: A discontinued GSK indole-class SARM studied for sarcopenia and androgen deficiency; never got past Phase I.

name: GSK-2849466
summary: A GSK SARM candidate for cachexia and heart failure that stopped after one small Phase I trial.

name: GTx-027
summary: A SARM candidate explored for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence; mostly preclinical, with no data on muscle or looks.

name: LY305
summary: A skin-applied SARM built for low testosterone and explored for muscle wasting; no appearance data.

name: PF-06260414
summary: Pfizer's oral SARM for cachexia; safety-tested in healthy men, then shelved.

name: JNJ-26146900
summary: A Johnson & Johnson SARM studied in rats as a prostate cancer drug, with anabolic effects on muscle and bone in animals; never given to humans.

name: EM-9017
summary: A steroidal SARM from Endorecherche patents, described in rats as supporting muscle while inhibiting prostate tissue.

name: RU-59063
summary: A 1990s research androgen-receptor ligand, sometimes classed as a SARM, that became a template for later antiandrogens; no human use.

name: Bolandiol
summary: A nandrolone-related steroid with mixed androgen, estrogen and progestin activity; raised lean mass in rats, never marketed as a base.

name: Dienolone
summary: A never-marketed nandrolone-like steroid, mainly of interest as a chemical intermediate.

name: Norclostebol
summary: A 1950s chlorinated nandrolone derivative described as strongly anabolic and weakly androgenic; no listed medical use and no human studies.

name: Oxabolone
summary: A nandrolone-family anabolic steroid that users associate with lean mass gain; it is banned in sport and little has been published on it.

name: SM-130686
summary: An experimental oral growth hormone secretagogue that works through the ghrelin receptor, discussed for leaner, fuller-looking physiques.

name: Bezafibrate
summary: A prescription lipid drug that activates PPAR receptors, discussed in fat-loss circles alongside PPAR-delta compounds for a leaner body.

name: Seladelpar
summary: An FDA-approved PPAR-delta agonist for a liver condition, followed in fat-loss circles because it hits the same target as GW501516.

name: Elafibranor
summary: An approved dual PPAR-alpha/delta agonist for a liver condition, mentioned in fat-loss talk because PPAR-delta is linked to fat burning.

name: GW0742
summary: A PPAR-delta research compound sold gray-market as 'Cardarine 2.0', taken in cutting phases for fat burning and endurance.

name: L-165041
summary: A lab PPAR-delta agonist from the GW501516 family, studied in cells and mice for how it shifts fat metabolism.

name: Acadesine
summary: An AMPK activator marketed as an exercise mimetic for fat burning and endurance without extra training.

name: SLU-PP-332
summary: An experimental ERR agonist billed as an exercise mimetic, with mouse results for endurance and less fat gain.

name: BAM-15
summary: A mitochondrial uncoupler that burns more calories as heat and cut fat in mice, discussed online as a 'safer DNP'.

name: Adipotide
summary: An experimental peptide that targets the blood vessels feeding fat tissue; it cut weight in monkeys and development stopped.

name: Fenfluramine
summary: A former prescription appetite suppressant, best known in fen-phen, withdrawn in 1997 and now a restricted epilepsy medicine.

name: Ephedrine/caffeine (ECA stack)
summary: A classic ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin cutting stack used for energy and appetite control while dieting down for a leaner look.

name: Zenagamtide
summary: Novo Nordisk's investigational GLP-1 plus amylin dual agonist (amycretin), with large weight loss reported in early trials.

name: Enicepatide
summary: Roche's weekly GLP-1/GIP dual agonist for weight loss, now in phase 3 and headed for a tirzepatide head-to-head.

name: CT-996
summary: Roche's experimental oral GLP-1 pill for weight loss, with registered phase 2 trials and no results published yet.

name: Petrelintide
summary: A weekly amylin-analogue obesity drug from Zealand and Roche that increases fullness for weight loss, now in phase 3.

name: Eloralintide
summary: Lilly's weekly amylin agonist, with roughly 9 to 20 percent weight loss reported at 48 weeks in phase 2.

name: Maridebart cafraglutide
summary: Amgen's monthly GLP-1 agonist / GIP-blocker injection, in phase 3, with roughly 12-16% weight loss at a year in phase 2.

name: Aleniglipron
summary: An experimental once-daily GLP-1 pill that cut weight by about 8-11% (placebo-adjusted) over 36 weeks in phase 2b.

name: ACCG-2671
summary: An early oral amylin-pathway pill for obesity, aimed at greater fullness and a leaner body; it is in first-in-human testing.

name: Elecoglipron
summary: AstraZeneca's once-daily GLP-1 pill that cut appetite and produced up to about 10% weight loss at 26 weeks in phase 2, helping a leaner body.

name: AZD6234
summary: AstraZeneca's long-acting amylin agonist injection for obesity, aimed at fullness and a leaner body; phase 3 is registered.

name: AZD9550
summary: AstraZeneca's experimental GLP-1/glucagon injection that targets appetite and energy use for fat loss; tested alone and with an amylin agonist.

name: Berobenatide
summary: Pfizer's investigational monthly GLP-1 injection for obesity, aimed at lower appetite and a leaner body; phase 3 trials are registered.

name: PF-08653945
summary: Pfizer's early-stage amylin analogue for obesity, aimed at fullness and a leaner body; no human results are published.

name: ABBV-295
summary: AbbVie's injectable amylin analogue for obesity, aimed at fullness and a leaner body, now in early trials.

name: Pramlintide
summary: An approved amylin-analogue injection for insulin-treated diabetes that slows digestion and boosts fullness; weight loss showed up in trials.

name: Dulaglutide
summary: A once-weekly GLP-1 injection for type 2 diabetes that lowers appetite and causes modest weight loss for a leaner body.

name: Lixisenatide
summary: A daily short-acting GLP-1 injection for type 2 diabetes that curbs appetite after meals, with slight weight loss.

name: Albiglutide
summary: A withdrawn once-weekly GLP-1 diabetes injection that lowered appetite and produced modest weight effects in trials.

name: Peptide YY
summary: A gut hormone released after meals that signals fullness and cut food intake in infusion studies, supporting a leaner physique.

name: Emugrobart
summary: An anti-myostatin antibody from Chugai/Roche tested to build or preserve muscle, including alongside weight-loss drugs.

name: ACE-031
summary: An experimental myostatin-blocking protein that raised muscle measures in healthy women and Duchenne boys; trials ended and it is not approved.

name: Stamulumab
summary: A discontinued Wyeth antibody that blocks myostatin to release the brake on muscle growth; tested in muscular dystrophy.

name: JA-16
summary: JA-16 is an experimental anti-myostatin antibody studied in animals as a way to increase muscle mass.

name: ARO-INHBE
summary: An experimental RNAi drug targeting INHBE to shift fat distribution toward a leaner midsection; early trials only.

name: ARO-ALK7
summary: An experimental RNAi drug targeting the ALK7 fat-cell receptor so fat cells release more stored fat; one early trial is recruiting.

name: WVE-007
summary: An experimental liver-targeted siRNA aimed at cutting visceral fat while keeping lean mass, for a leaner, more defined look; early company data.

name: ALN-6222
summary: An experimental INHBE-targeting RNAi drug aimed at shifting fat distribution; it has just entered its first obesity trial.

name: Monlunabant
summary: An experimental oral CB1 blocker that lowers appetite for weight loss; Phase 2 showed modest results with some neuropsychiatric side effects.

name: CRB-913
summary: An experimental CB1 blocker that boosted the weight loss of GLP-1 drugs in obese mice; human results are not yet public.

name: Nimacimab
summary: An experimental anti-CB1 antibody in Phase 2 for obesity, aimed at lowering appetite and fat storage for a leaner body.

name: NAD+ injections
aka: NAD+ IV, NAD+ shots, coenzyme I
summary: Injected or infused NAD+ is used in longevity clinics for energy and anti-aging, with users hoping for fresher, more youthful-looking skin.

name: Glutathione injections
summary: Injected glutathione, often with vitamin C, is used in some countries to lighten skin and even out tone.

name: VIP (Vasoactive intestinal peptide)
summary: A natural vasodilating neuropeptide sold as a research peptide; users speculate it could aid circulation and recovery.

name: Aviptadil
summary: Synthetic VIP used with phentolamine for erectile dysfunction in some countries and tested in COVID-19 lung failure.

name: Ara-290
summary: An EPO-derived repair peptide tested in small neuropathy trials, discussed by users for tissue protection and recovery.

name: B7-33
summary: A lab-made relaxin mimic studied in animals for fibrosis; peptide communities discuss it for tissue repair and scar reduction.

name: PE-22-28
summary: A spadin-derived peptide studied in rodents as a fast-acting antidepressant; some users discuss it for mood and confidence.

name: PNC-27
summary: A p53-derived peptide reported to rupture cancer cells in lab studies, sold as a research chemical to longevity-minded users.

name: Erythropoietin
summary: A kidney hormone and anaemia drug used for endurance doping; raises red blood cells for stamina, with serious cardiovascular warnings.

name: Abaloparatide
summary: An approved osteoporosis bone-builder that forum users discuss for facial structure and height alongside bonesmashing and lengthening.

name: Salmon calcitonin
summary: A fish-derived calcitonin used for Paget's disease and high blood calcium that slows bone breakdown to preserve bone.

name: Osteocalcin
summary: A bone-made protein and proposed hormone linked to bone formation, insulin and muscle in animal studies.

name: Irisin
summary: A proposed exercise hormone released from muscle that turns white fat brown-like in mice, linking training to leanness.

name: Adropin
summary: A liver and brain peptide linked in mice to fat and glucose metabolism; human data are blood-level associations.

name: Asprosin
summary: A fat-derived fasting hormone that raises glucose and appetite in mice; high levels track with obesity.

name: Obestatin
summary: A ghrelin-gene peptide first reported in 2005 to curb appetite; follow-up work has questioned both the effect and its receptor.

name: Erythroferrone
summary: The hormone red blood cell precursors release to lower hepcidin and free up iron, supporting oxygen delivery and recovery.

name: Limostatin
summary: A fruit-fly hormone that lowers insulin during fasting, studied as a model for how fasting signals shape fat handling.

name: Alamandine
summary: A blood-pressure-regulating peptide of the renin-angiotensin system, studied in rodents for heart and vessel protection.

name: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone
summary: The hypothalamic hormone that tells the pituitary to release TSH, setting thyroid activity, metabolism and energy.

name: Montirelin
summary: A lab-stable TRH analogue people discuss for alertness and energy that keeps training and routines consistent; studied in animals for arousal.

name: Glypromate
summary: GPE, a small IGF-1-derived peptide studied for brain protection and recovery; its analogue trofinetide became an approved Rett syndrome drug.

name: Trofinetide
summary: An oral prescription drug for Rett syndrome and an analogue of GPE; it is a disease treatment, with no appearance use documented.

name: Fosgonimeton
summary: An investigational Alzheimer's drug that acts as a prodrug of dihexa, developed for cognition rather than appearance.

name: BNN-20
summary: A DHEA-derived BDNF-mimicking compound studied in Parkinson's mouse models for brain protection.

name: BNN-27
summary: A DHEA-derived NGF-mimicking compound studied in cells and mice for nerve and brain protection.

name: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate
summary: An acetylated, amidated Selank analogue sold as a research chemical for calmer mood and social ease.

name: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate
summary: An acetylated, amidated Semax analogue sold as a research chemical for sharper focus and stamina.

name: P21
summary: A CNTF-derived nootropic peptide studied in mice for memory and neurogenesis and used by enthusiasts for focus.

name: DNSP-11
summary: An experimental GDNF-derived brain peptide studied in rats and monkeys for dopamine neuron support.

name: FGL
summary: A lab-made fragment of a neural adhesion protein studied in rodents for memory and brain plasticity.

name: Cenegermin
summary: A prescription nerve growth factor eye drop approved for a rare corneal disease; it is a medical treatment with no appearance use.

name: Mecasermin rinfabate
summary: An IGF-1/IGFBP-3 injectable built for rare growth failure in children; no data covers height in people with normal growth.

name: Axokine
summary: A discontinued CNTF-based injectable developed for obesity that produced modest weight loss in trials.

name: Glycyl-prolyl-hydroxyproline
summary: A collagen-derived tripeptide found in oral collagen supplements, which people take for skin firmness and hydration.

name: AHK-Cu
summary: A copper tripeptide marketed in hair-care products for thicker, fuller hair, studied so far in cultured follicle cells.

name: LL-37
summary: The body's own antimicrobial skin peptide, discussed for clearing acne and healing skin.

name: Heberprot-P
summary: A Cuban injectable EGF used for diabetic foot ulcers, and a reference point in discussions of EGF for skin healing.

name: Palifermin
summary: A prescription keratinocyte growth factor that protects mouth and gut lining in cancer treatment, mentioned in skin-renewal discussions.
